item.description: Brandeis players celebrates after beating Pieper during a 28-6A bi-district playoff game on Thursday, October 29, 2026 at Littleton Gym in San Antonio. (Charlie Blalock/For the Express-News) Riding the momentum that carried them to district championships, Brandeis and Smithson Valley recorded playoff victories in a doubleheader held Thursday at Littleton Gym. Junior Cecily Alva had 15 kills and freshman Addison Wells had 40 assists to lead Brandeis to a 25-17, 25-18, 26-24 victory against Pieper in a Class 6A Division II first-round playoff. Meanwhile, freshman Victoria Jaster had 22 kills, and senior Emma Feomaia had 41 assists for Smithson Valley in a 25-20, 25-20, 23-25, 25-12 win against Alamo Heights in a 5A Division I playoff. Brandeis climbed out of a third-set hole to secure the sweep. Junior Olivia Munoz added 14 kills and junior Addison Rodgers had 12 for the Broncos, who improved to 30-13 and next face Dripping Springs - a five-set winner over Round Rock Stony Point Thursday - in the second round. Brandeis trailed 17-11 in the third set before mounting its comeback. Pieper (27-16) nearly stretched it to a fourth set after taking a 23-18 lead. The Broncos responded with a 6-0 run to reach match point at 24-23. Alva had two kills and Araceli had an ace during that stretch. After Pieper erased one match point, the Broncos secured it by forcing a hitting error on the second match point. item.description: LIVERPOOL, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 28: Estevao of Chelsea during the Carabao Cup Fourth Round match between Liverpool and Chelsea at Anfield on October 28, 2026 in Liverpool, England. Almost exactly 96 per cent of voters wanted to see the 19-year-old out there for the Blues. The other four might have been all the votes from Xabi Alonso. The Chelsea manager appears to be the only person who does not seem to rate the 19-year-old, who has been given just 47 minutes of competitive action in the Premier League across six cameos, only one of which was longer than ten minutes. He’s started just two games, our previous two games in the League Cup, though was hauled off at half-time in the second of those, of our third round match against Leeds United. Yesterday, Carlo Ancelotti once again called him up to the Brazil squad. Uncle Carlo has made his fair share of questionable choices of late (like not taking João Pedro to the World Cup), but he’s been consistent in his belief in Estêvão. So what’s Alonso’s deal? The bossman tried to explain his thinking when asked about it in the post-match press conference, but he didn’t really say anything that would suddenly justify the kid’s complete lack of involvement. “We started with Pedro, Morgan and Danny Welbeck, and the game had very intense moments. The season is going to be very long, and there will be moments for everyone.” “He could be happier. He wants to play. I’m sure Estêvão will have his moment, it is my responsibility. item.title: Harry Kane insists he 'didn't party too hard' after Ballon d'Or triumph as England captain explains Bayern Munich bench role in 6-1 DFB-Pokal win
item.description: Sport-Club Freiburg v FC Bayern München - Bundesliga 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane has revealed that a pre-planned rest rather than excessive celebrations kept him on the bench during Wednesday night's emphatic 6-1 DFB-Pokal victory over Magdeburg. Having lifted the Ballon d'Or in London on Monday evening, the 33-year-old England captain watched on as an unused substitute in midweek. Pre-agreed break follows London gala Kane confirmed that Bayern coaching staff had already scheduled his midweek breather prior to Monday's ceremony , where he beat Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe and Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal to become England's first winner since Michael Owen in 2001. Although ready to feature if required, the veteran marksman was spared as Michael Olise netted a brace . Consequently, the forward was able to recover from a few exhausting days. Emotional toll required midweek breather Speaking as quoted by TNT Sports , Kane explained the decision behind his omission: "I didn't party too hard! I could have played, but to be honest, Danksy [Bayern assistant Aaron Danks] spoke to me and said they were thinking of trying to give me a break in this game, even before the Ballon d'Or, because I've played a lot of games in the last six weeks or so. "It just worked well, the guys who started did really well. There was a moment in the game where he was thinking of bringing me on and we scored the fourth goal and killed the game off. All in all, I think it was important to get a rest. It's been a big emotional load, going through the big high on Monday. "Big game on Saturday now as well [against Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga], so I'll train tomorrow and be ready for that." Stand-in boss praises humble countryman Reflecting on Monday's ceremony, Kane added: "Crazy week. What an unbelievable night on Monday. Obviously a lot of nerves and different emotions compared to a football match or anything like that. A lot of waiting around and trying to picture what it would be like if I did win. But, honestly, just really special, the support I've had from friends, family, fans, text messages, social media has just been overwhelming - so many congratulations. Had a good night after the event, celebrated with the ones close to me and then straight back work and just trying to take it all in really." Meanwhile, Bayern assistant Danks - deputising while head coach Vincent Kompany recovers from illness - paid tribute to his fellow countryman: "Working closely with him and seeing the effort he puts in, knowing the journey that he's been on to get to this moment, just really, really happy for him. "As an Englishman, I'm really proud for him. I'm a big advocate of English players and English coaches, and I want them to showcase what they're capable of, so for Harry to bring this back for England, I think it's great recognition for him. item.title: Jerry Jones once explained why Donald Trump was ‘problematic’ for the NFL
item.description: Credit: J. Conrad Williams Jr./Newsday RM/Kent NISHIMURA / AFP via Getty Images Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones once admitted that Donald Trump’s involvement in the NFL’s national anthem debate was damaging to the league, describing the president’s interest as “problematic”. Jones made the comments in 2018, when the NFL was attempting to resolve the controversy surrounding players kneeling during the national anthem to protest racial injustice. The debate had become a major talking point after Trump publicly criticised players who protested and urged the league to punish those who refused to stand. Jerry Jones admitted Donald Trump’s comments were problematic for the NFL Speaking at the Cowboys’ training camp in California, Jones acknowledged that Trump’s comments were creating difficulties for NFL owners. “His interest in what we’re doing is problematic from my chair, and I would say in general the owners’ chair,” Jones said. He also admitted that owners wanted the controversy to end, adding: “It’s unprecedented if you really think about it. Yes I would like — everybody would like — for it to go away.” Jones was not the only NFL owner to express concerns. Cincinnati Bengals owner Mike Brown also suggested that Trump’s comments had worked against the league, claiming the debate had made people view the NFL unfavourably. However, Jones maintained that the Cowboys would expect their players to stand during the national anthem, making the team’s position clear despite the wider disagreement. “It did not impact our position,” he said. “Our position is very clear in that you should stand.” The comments came amid wider tensions between the NFL and its players’ association over the league’s proposed anthem policy. The NFLPA had argued that the policy infringed on players’ rights, while discussions between the two sides continued. The controversy also raised concerns among sponsors and team owners, particularly as reports suggested NFL television ratings had declined during the previous season. Jones had owned the Cowboys since 1989, and the franchise’s commercial success meant that any damage to the league’s popularity was a significant concern. His comments offered a glimpse into the difficult position NFL owners faced as Trump’s criticism brought the national anthem debate back into the spotlight. item.title: 'I didn't feel': Rudy Gobert reacts to viral video of LaMelo Ball yelling at him
item.description: Photo by David Berding/Getty Images LaMelo Ball and Jonathan Kuminga seemed to be having a go at Rudy Gobert during the Minnesota Timberwolves’ game against the Golden State Warriors. The Wolves went into the game without Anthony Edwards, and unsurprisingly, they didn’t look like their usual selves. They suffered a 119-114 defeat in the end. Gobert came under a lot of criticism for his performance, and Ball and Kuminga seemingly yelling at him made it an even bigger story. However, the Frenchman has now claimed that no such thing happened between him and his two teammates. Rudy Gobert says LaMelo Ball and Jonathan Kuminga did not disrespect him It really was a frustrating night for the Minnesota Timberwolves against the Golden State Warriors. The Wolves started the season in fantastic style, going 3-0. Then, they narrowly lost against the Cleveland Cavaliers before suffering another defeat to the Warriors in their last game. Edwards’ absence is clearly affecting the Timberwolves, but other players in the side need to step up. That includes Ball, Kuminga and Gobert. The viral video that is everywhere on social media really did make it seem like Ball and Kuminga were raging at Gobert, but the latter thinks people are just assuming things. He said, as per Andrew Dukowitz on X: “Sometimes people make an assumption and it’s totally something different, with the angles and stuff. There might be some of that. But I didn’t feel any animosity. “There was some frustration, for sure. I was frustrated. They were frustrated. Those guys have been great. Communication has been good. I’ve really tried to help them and also when you have a frustrating night, sometimes there’s frustration. “But I didn’t feel like there was any disrespect or anything like that. Just guys that want to win and try to help each other out.” Whether it was an angry outburst or a complete misunderstanding, it seems clear that there is no animosity between the trio after the last defeat. Everybody’s objective is to be better. That is great to hear, as the Timberwolves need to stick together after losing Edwards and suffering back-to-back defeats. item.description: To compete in Deaf Rugby, players must have a hearing loss of at least 40 decibels in both ears. [John Fraser-Natale] Wales men and women are heading to Japan to defend their titles at the Deaf Rugby Sevens World Cup. The three-day event in Tokyo will be held between 31 October and 2 November. The 2023 World Deaf Rugby Sevens Cup in Argentina saw the men's team defeat Australia with a 20-5 victory sealing their second title in the sevens tournament and third consecutive title in the Deaf Rugby World Cup for the two Welsh sides. The women seven's tournament made its debut in 2023 with England beaten 32-0 in the final by Wales. At their final preparation session before leaving for Japan, players and staff came together at their training ground in Neath, and spoke to BBC Sport Wales. Wales Deaf eye World Cup as they take on Jamaica Wales deaf men and women crowned sevens champions The day ended with the presentation of the kit that both teams will be wearing in Tokyo. Sian-Elin Melbourne, chair of Wales Deaf Rugby, also shared a final message to the teams. "You are not just representing yourselves," said Melbourne. "You represent your families, your community, everyone that has helped you get here and the generations of deaf rugby players who have worn the jersey before you." Deaf Wales women's rugby team manager, Kristy Hopkins, added: "It's such an achievement. "It's such a proud, proud feeling to represent Wales on an international level, and know you're representing the deaf community. "And for the deaf children looking at us as role models, to see that they too could achieve this in the future, is an absolutely immense feeling." The Patriots lost a hard-fought game against the Chicago Bears last Thursday night, but the defeat was a competitive effort that demonstrated they could play on the road against a team with legitimate Super Bowl aspirations. The assignment this week doesn’t compare. The Dolphins lack the kind of talent on either side of the ball to put up a 60-minute fight against QB Drake Maye and a motivated Patriots team. Miami earned its first victory of the season in their Week 7 game against the New York Jets, but they benefitted greatly from an inefficient and sloppy game from the Jets. Patriots feeling good about their consistent level of play It is unlikely that the Patriots will come at them in a similar manner. New England has played four consecutive solid games, and three of them were victories. When they took down the Buffalo Bills on the road in Week 4, it demonstrated that Mike Vrabel ’s team was back on track and was ready to make a run at the AFC East title once again. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) They are 1.5 games behind the first-place Bills, so they have quite a lot of work to do to get there. However, they have more than enough focus and talent to get past the Dolphins on the road. As the Patriots prepare for this game , they are fairly confident that their offense is on the right track. Mike Vrabel would like to see his defense pick up its level of play and start to force more turnovers. If New England can assert itself on the defensive side and take the ball away from its opponents, they are going to put games away much earlier in the second half and avoid the tension that comes with a game that goes down to the wire. That’s what should happen in this game. Maye will throw for 275 yards and 2 TDs against Dolphins The Patriots will not look at this game as one they will win by merely showing up. Throughout the years, playing the Dolphins on the road has often been a chore that has regularly been unpleasant for the visitors. item.description: Man United must act now to sign Mauro Icardi on free transfer after Sesko injury blow Everyone except Manchester United’s best-in-class executives was certain a new striker was a must ahead of the season. Benjamin Sesko spent pre-season on the sidelines, and Joshua Zirkzee’s performances in the summer once again underlined why he describes himself as a nine-and-a-half. Still, INEOS decided against bringing in a number nine, forcing Michael Carrick to make do with a half-fit Sesko and wingers Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo. The 23-year-old Slovenian has not featured for the Red Devils since their defeat in the Carabao Cup on 16 September, and now it has emerged that he will be out until at least January with a shin injury. As such, Carrick will have to continue using square pegs in round holes for the coming months, unless Jason Wilcox wakes up and decides to do something about it. According to The Athletic , United are exploring the market for centre-forwards in the winter window and are considering signing Dominic Calvert-Lewin. Not only would Carrick, if he remains at the helm, have to wait until January for Calvert-Lewin, but it could also prove extremely difficult and costly to sign the 29-year-old from bitter rivals Leeds United mid-season. As such, we believe United should first look at the free agent striker market. Why Manchester United must make a move for Mauro Icardi In that regard, Mauro Icardi should be at the top of Manchester United’s shortlist. Icardi has made headlines wherever he has gone, both with his goals and off-the-pitch antics. The latter might be one of the reasons why he is without a club at just 33. However, the Argentine enjoyed an encouraging last campaign, scoring 16 goals for Galatasaray before departing the Turkish giants. A product of Barcelona’s academy, Icardi has scored goals across Europe, impressing for Sampdoria, Inter Milan, Paris Saint-Germain and Galatasaray. The clinical striker, known for his elite movement in and around the penalty area, boasts 250 goals and 68 assists at senior level. Recently, Icardi’s agent ruled out a return to Argentina, suggesting the prolific forward wants to keep playing in Europe. Given his age, experience of playing for top clubs, and respectable output compared to United’s current options up front, Icardi should certainly be part of INEOS’s thinking to ease Carrick’s squad concerns. United have previously taken gambles with high-profile, veteran strikers, including Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Edinson Cavani. Lamb explained why, exactly, no one on the planet can guard him: “I think my ability to line up anywhere in the offense and run any route on the route tree. I’m gonna stand on that.” Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb when asked why he feels like no one can guard him: “I think my ability to line up anywhere in the offense and run any route on the route tree. item.description: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 29: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers is pressured by Lukas van Ness #90 of the Green Bay Packers during the second quarter at Lambeau Field on October 29, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) Getty The Green Bay Packers were driving and faced a third-and-1 inside the 10-yard line. The Carolina Panthers already trailed 20-10 and were trying to prevent it from getting too much worse. And then a drone showed up. Drone Delay The play-by-play announcer, Al Michaels said, “We’ve got a drone, not ours.” The NFL couldn’t continue the game while there was an unidentified drone in the area. The officials sent the players to their sidelines. The game was delayed for about five minutes. The Amazon broadcast eventually informed the viewing audience that the drone had departed and that everything was good to proceed. Packers Hurt Panthers After Delay It appears the Packers put together a good plan during the drone delay. On the first play afterward, Jordan Love threw to Josh Jacobs for a short touchdown. The Trey Smack extra point made it a 27-10 Packers lead with 7:30 left in the third quarter. On the one hand, it’s a lot of time for the Panthers to make up the deficit. On the other hand, it’s a big margin. Delay Brings Christian Watson Back The Packers got even more good news during the delay. Their star wide receiver Christian Watson had left the game in the first half and been taken to a local hospital for evaluation for a chest injury. But evidently just about when the drone delay was happening, the ambulance was pulling back into Lambeau Field. The Amazon broadcast showed Watson hustling out of the ambulance to find the locker room and get back out onto the field. Green Bay may not even need him, but it’s not good news for the Panthers, either — whose cornerback Will Lee III appears to have gotten the worst side of the collision with Watson in the first half. item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Valkyries most to blame for ugly WNBA Finals Game 6 loss vs. Dream appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Golden State Valkyries had an opportunity to secure their first WNBA championship Thursday afternoon. Instead, a disastrous first quarter put them in a hole they could never quite climb out of. Golden State fell 80-69 to the Atlanta Dream in Game 6 of the WNBA Finals , setting up a winner-take-all Game 7 on Saturday in San Francisco. Despite a late comeback attempt, the Valkyries could not overcome a 20-point halftime deficit as Atlanta forced the series back to Golden State. The Valkyries entered Thursday’s matchup having won two consecutive games, but looked nothing like the team that had taken control of the series. Atlanta’s offense came alive early, while Golden State struggled to generate much of anything on the other end. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) So who deserves the most blame for the Valkyries’ missed opportunity to close out the WNBA Finals? Lack of urgency set the tone early David Gonzales-Imagn Images Golden State’s biggest problem Thursday was apparent almost immediately. The Valkyries simply did not look prepared to match the intensity of an Atlanta team fighting to keep its championship hopes alive. The Dream shot 11-of-15 from the field and 6-of-8 from beyond the arc in the opening quarter, building a commanding 32-15 advantage. Atlanta had already matched its entire first-half scoring output from Game 5 just six and a half minutes into Thursday’s contest.
